issues.description: The solution implementation declares private attributes using snake_case names (e.g., lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor, getters, setters, and other methods use camelCase field names (e.g., lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This mismatch between declared field identifiers and the identifiers used throughout the class causes compilation errors and contradicts the UML/problem statement that uses camelCase names, making the provided solution unusable and confusing for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the declared private fields use the same camelCase identifiers as in the UML and the rest of the class (e.g., private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors;), or alternatively update all usages to match the snake_case declarations. Prefer aligning declarations to the UML/problem statement (camelCase) so constructor and methods compile and match the exercise specification.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify attribute names using camelCase (e.g. lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), but the solution implementation declares the private fields using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while the constructor and methods in the same solution file refer to the camelCase identifiers. This creates a naming mismatch between the problem/UML and the provided solution and also an internal inconsistency inside the solution file, which can confuse students trying to map the UML requirements to the example solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the private fields in the solution to use the camelCase identifiers specified in the UML/problem: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. Ensure all uses (constructor assignments, getters/setters, methods) consistently reference these camelCase fields.
